newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia regulator revokes Fumakilla listing.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia regulator revokes Fumakilla listing.

text.p: Malaysia's Securities Commission on Thursday announced it was withdrawing Fumakilla Malaysia Bhd's approval to list on the Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange (KLSE).
"The Securities Commission (SC) has today revoked its approval for the listing on the Second Board of the Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange of Fumakilla," the stock market watchdog said in a statement.
It said Fumakilla has been found to have made misleading statements to the SC in its listing application.
"The SC was misled on the actual and beneficial Bumiputra (ethnic Malay) shareholding in Fumakilla," the SC said.
Under a government policy, all publicly listed companies should have at least 30 percent of their equity held by Bumiputras.
The SC did not exactly say how Fumakilla had flouted this requirement.
It said it could also take further action against the company under the Securities Commission Act.
The SC decision follows a probe into the company announced on November 25, just ahead of the balloting of the company's public issue applications.
The balloting was scheduled for Wednesday.
Fumakilla had on offer six million ordinary shares at a price of 3.20 ringgit per share.
